spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The decisive comparison is between a height-only Stieltjes sum and a zero-sum invariant: functional symmetry fixes the latter, while strict equality in a paired convexity bound detects whether every real part is one-half.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The xi Hadamard product gives B=-Σρ 1/ρ and, after conjugate pairing, a real zero sum. Integrating G(x)=(1/4+x²)^-1 against dN(x) produces Σ(1/4+T²)^-1; pairing σ with 1-σ and applying the stated convexity inequality makes equality with -B occur exactly at σ=1/2.
directed.conceptual_reading: The kernel deliberately forgets real parts, and the invariant restores a comparison target; equality rather than mere value matching carries the critical-line information.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The zero-counting measure dN converts critical zeros into a Stieltjes sum, while Hadamard factorization and convexity connect that sum to a critical-line condition.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The argument relies on symmetry-paired zeros and strict equality conditions, not on computing N alone; the source's phrase about unconditionality is awkward and should not be used to strengthen the claim.
directed.uncertainty: The rational kernels and zero sums are formula-sensitive, but the equality mechanism is recoverable from prose.

supported: The span derives a height-only Stieltjes sum and compares it with the Hadamard zero-sum constant using paired zeros.
The displayed inequality has equality only at σ=1/2, which is the intended RH-discriminating mechanism.
inference: The description of the height kernel as forgetting real parts and the invariant as supplying a comparison target is well grounded.
unsupported_or_imported: Calling the mechanism convexity is mathematically inaccurate: for T>1, f_T(σ)=σ/(σ²+T²) is concave on [0,1], consistent with the displayed midpoint-maximizing inequality. The source itself uses the wrong word, and the candidate repeats it without flagging the error.
context_or_ocr_risk: The source's phrase 'unconditionally upon RH' is internally contradictory; the candidate appropriately avoids strengthening it.
missed_mechanism: The candidate misses that the source's convexity label is erroneous even though the inequality and equality case remain usable.
revision_instructions: Replace 'convexity' with the stated paired inequality, or explicitly call it a concavity/midpoint-maximization argument for T>1; retain equality iff σ=1/2 and flag the source's terminology error.

after.text:
In this paper, we make no claim to producing a solution to the Riemann hypothesis. We
believe that rephrasing it as a problem in physics renders it more tractable and constitutes
an advance in its own right. While string theory presents a model for quantum gravity, much
of its considerable success to date has been in connecting physics to mathematics and linking
different areas of mathematics to each other. Indeed, many areas of string theory fall under
the rubric of physical mathematics [38]. The Riemann hypothesis resides at the nexus of
number theory, analysis, and geometry. It is therefore completely natural that string theory
and the Riemann hypothesis couple to each other as well.
